'''Shasta''' is an extinct [[Shastan languages|Shastan language]] formerly spoken from northern California into southwestern Oregon. It was spoken in a number of dialects, possibly including [[Okwanuchu language|Okwanuchu]]. The last fluent speaker, Clara Wicks, died in 1978,<ref name="Golla" /> and by 1980, only two first language speakers, both elderly, were alive. Today, all ethnic Shasta people speak English as their first language.

== Name ==
{{See also|Shasta people#Origin of name}}
The origins of the term "Shasta" are vague; the Shasta called themselves "{{Lang|sht|Kahosadi}}" (plain speakers).<ref>{{cite book|last=Holt|first=Catherine|editor-last=Kroeber|editor-first=Alfred|title=Shasta Ethnography|series=Anthropological Records|publisher=University of California Press|volume=3|pages=301–302|year=1946|url=http://dpg.lib.berkeley.edu/webdb/anthpubs/search?all=&volume=3&journal=3&item=5|access-date=28 January 2018 }}</ref> [[Peter Skene Ogden]] is the first recorded Euro-American to have used a variation of the term "Shasta", which he spelled "Sastise," "Castice," "Sistise," "Sarti," and "Sasty".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Miesse |first=William C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xBASAQAAIAAJ |title=Mount Shasta: An Annotated Bibliography |date=1993 |publisher=College of the Siskiyous |pages=116 |language=en |chapter=The Name 'Shasta'}}</ref>

* {{lang|sht|Ikirakácˑu}} ([[Oregon]] Shasta)
* {{lang|sht|Iruhikwáˑcˑu}} ([[Klamath River]] Shasta)

* {{lang|sht|Ahútˑireˀeˑcˑu}} ([[Shasta River|Shasta Valley]] Shasta)

The length of a consonant distinguishes meaning in Shasta words. All stops, fricatives and nasals can occur as long or short in Shasta, but approximants {{IPA|/r j w/}} only occur as short consonants.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Silver |first=Shirley |title=The Shasta Language |date=1966 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=University of California |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6hj0n3zb |pages=37–38}}</ref> [[Minimal pair]]s and near minimal pairs are shown below:

* {{IPA|/t͡ʃá'''k'''àráx/}} ''a gnat'' vs. {{IPA|/t͡sà'''kː'''írʔ/}} ''a board''
* {{IPA|/ʔá'''tʼ'''ùʔ/}} ''nothing'' vs. {{IPA|/ʔá'''tʼː'''ùʔ/}} ''wild sunflower''
* {{IPA|/ʔì'''s'''íkʼːàʔ/}} ''a person'' vs. {{IPA|/ʔì'''sː'''íkʼ/}} ''cold''

=== Tones ===
Shasta vowels can have low or high tones. High tones are marked by an acute accent {{angbr|′}} in the orthography devised by Silver (1966), whereas low tones are left unmarked. Examples for the vowel {{IPA|/u/}} are given below:

==Orthography==
Silver (1966) devised a spelling system for distinguishing consonants and vowels in Shasta. Long phonemes are represented with the symbol {{angbr|ˑ}} following the character (e.g. {{angbr|cˑ}} and {{angbr|eˑ}} for {{IPA|/t͡sː/}} and {{IPA|/eː/}}, respectively); [[ejective]]s are indicated by an apostrophe written over the character (e.g. {{angbr|p̓}} for {{IPA|/pʼ/}}). The phoneme {{IPA|/j/}} is represented by {{angbr|y}}, and the glottal stop {{IPA|/ʔ/}} is represented by the superscript IPA symbol {{angbr|ˀ}}. The letters {{angbr|b d f g j l q v z}} are not used to represent Shasta sounds.
